tier1_canonical.basis: Met-/Leu-enkephalin YGGFM/YGGFL, beta-endorphin YGGFMTSEK..., dynorphin A YGGFLRRIRPKLK, N/OFQ FGGFTGARK... (F anchor)
bovine beta-casomorphins YPFP/YPFPG/YPFPGPI, human YPFV, soymorphin YPFVVN, neocasomorphin YPVEPF, endomorphin-1 YPWF, casoxin B YPYY
casoxin A YPSYGLN, casoxin-6 SRYPSY (internal site)
alpha-lactorphin YGLF, beta-lactorphin YLLF, lactoferroxin A YLGSGY

tier2_aromatic_pair.basis: docs/structural_basis.md 4: YGGF, YPW, Y[D-Ala]F and FGGF share one aromatic pocket

screening_targets.rule: tier 1 motif, released as peptide N-terminus, length >= 4, deduplicated by sequence

caveats: Tier 2 is permissive by construction (aromatic anchor + second aromatic at +2/+3) and a tier-2 hit is a hypothesis, not a prediction. Only tier 1 becomes a screening target.
A motif site is evidence of a potential N-terminus, not of release. The released_nterminal set is the only one with peptidomic evidence behind it.
Nothing here measures binding. The atlas selects what is worth scoring.
Peptides are mapped to parents by exact substring match, so a peptide shared between two parents is reported against both.
